text:
Two liquids of densities $ρ_{1}$ and $ρ_{2}$ ($ρ_{2}$ = 2$ρ_{1}$) are
filled up behind a square wall of side 10 m as
shown in figure. Each liquid has a height of
5 m. The ratio of the forces due to these liquids
exerted on upper part MN to that at the lower part
NO is (Assume that the liquids are not mixing)

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The liquids do not mix, so the denser liquid ($ρ_{2}=2ρ_{1}$) occupies the lower part NO and the lighter liquid ($ρ_{1}$) the upper part MN. Each part has height $h=5\text{m}$ and area $A=10\times 5\text{m}^{2}$. Atmospheric pressure acts on both faces of the wall, so only gauge pressure counts.

On MN the pressure rises linearly from $0$ at M to $ρ_{1}gh$ at N, so the average pressure is $\dfrac{ρ_{1}gh}{2}$:

$F_{1}=\dfrac{ρ_{1}gh}{2}A$

On NO the pressure rises linearly from $ρ_{1}gh$ at N to $ρ_{1}gh+ρ_{2}gh=3ρ_{1}gh$ at O, so the average pressure is $2ρ_{1}gh$:

$F_{2}=2ρ_{1}ghA$

$\dfrac{F_{1}}{F_{2}}=\dfrac{ρ_{1}gh/2}{2ρ_{1}gh}=\dfrac{1}{4}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot

text:
A particle of mass m is dropped from a height
h above the ground. At the same time another
particle of the same mass is thrown vertically
upwards from the ground with a speed of $\sqrt{2gh}$. If they collide head-on completely
inelastically, the time taken for the combined
mass to reach the ground, in units of $\sqrt{\frac{h}{g}}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Particles will collide after time t = $\frac{h}{\sqrt{2gh}}$ = $\sqrt{\frac{h}{2g}}$

Velocity of (A) just before collision, 
$V_{A} = 0 + gt =$ $g\sqrt{\frac{h}{2g}}$ = $\sqrt{\frac{gh}{2}}$

Velocity of (B) just before collision, 

$V_{B} =$ $\sqrt{2gh}$ - $g\sqrt{\frac{h}{2g}}$ 

= $\sqrt{2gh}$ - $\sqrt{\frac{gh}{2}}$

= $\sqrt{gh}\left [\sqrt{2}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]$

As 'mg' is non-impulsive so conserving linear momentum just before and just after collision,

$P_{i} = P_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ m$\sqrt{gh}\left [\sqrt{2}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]$ - m$\sqrt{\frac{gh}{2}}$ = $2mV_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ $V_{f} = 0$

height from ground where collision
 takes place $= h_{1} = h -$ $\frac{1}{2}gt^{2}$ = h - $\frac{1}{2}g.\frac{h}{2g}$ = $\frac{3h}{4}$

Time taken by combined mass to reach the

ground = $\sqrt{\frac{2\times \frac{3h}{4}}{2g}}$ = $\sqrt{\frac{3h}{2g}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot

text:
An electron (mass m) with initial velocity $\vec{v}=v_{0}\hat{i}+v_{0}\hat{j}$ is in an electric field $\vec{E}=-E_{0}\widehat{k}$. If $λ_{0}$ is initial de-Broglie wavelength of electron,
its de-Broglie wave length at time t is given
by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{v}=v_{0}\hat{i}+v_{0}\hat{j}$

$λ_{0}$ = $\frac{h}{m\sqrt{2}v_{0}}$ ....(1)

$\vec{E}=-E_{0}\widehat{k}$

$\vec{F}=q\vec{E}$ = (-e)($-E_{0}\widehat{k}$) = $eE_{0}\widehat{k}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{a}=\frac{\vec{F}}{m}$ = $\frac{eE_{0}\widehat{k}}{m}$

Velocity at time t, 

$\vec{v_{f}}$ = $v_{0}\hat{i}+v_{0}\hat{j}$ + $\frac{eE_{0}}{m}t\widehat{k}$

 $\left |\vec{v_{f}}\right |$ = $\sqrt{v_{0}^{2}+v_{0}^{2}+\left (\frac{eE_{0}t}{m}\right )^{2}}$

= $\sqrt{2v_{0}^{2}+\frac{e^{2}E_{0}^{2}}{m^{2}}t^{2}}$

$\therefore$ Wavelength at time t

$λ$ = $\frac{h}{mv_{f}}$ = $\frac{h}{m\sqrt{2v_{0}^{2}+\frac{e2E2 0}{m2}t^{2}}}$

= $\frac{h}{\sqrt{2}mv_{0}\sqrt{1+\frac{e2E2 0}{2m2v2 0}t^{2}}}$

= $\frac{λ_{0}}{\sqrt{1+\frac{e2E2 0}{2m2v2 0}t^{2}}}$

text:
A particle moves such that its position
vector $\vec{r}(t)=\cos ωt\hat{i}+\sin ωt\hat{j}$ where $ω$ is a constant and t is time. Then which of the following statements is true for the velocity
$\vec{v}(t)$ and acceleration $\vec{a}(t)$ of the particle :
options:
$\vec{v}$ is perpendicular to  $\vec{r}$ and $\vec{a}$ is directed
towards the origin

$\vec{v}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{r}$ and $\vec{a}$ is directed
away from the origin
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{r}(t)=\cos ωt\hat{i}+\sin ωt\hat{j}$

$\vec{v}=\frac{d\vec{r}}{dt}$ = $-ω\sin ωt\hat{i}+ω\cos ωt\hat{j}$

$\vec{a}=\frac{d\vec{v}}{dt}$ = $-ω^{2}\cos ωt\hat{i}-ω^{2}\sin ωt\hat{j}$

= $-ω^{2}\left (\cos ωt\hat{i}+\sin ωt\hat{j}\right )$

= $-ω^{2}\vec{r}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{a}$
 is antiparallel to $\vec{r}$ and it's direction towards the origin.

$\vec{v}.\vec{r}=$ $ω(-\sin ωt\cos ωt+\cos ωt\sin ωt)$ = 0

So $\vec{v}⊥\vec{r}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot

text:
A ball is dropped from the top of a 100 m high
tower on a planet. In the last $\frac{1}{2}s$ before hitting
the ground, it covers a distance of 19 m.
Acceleration due to gravity (in $ms^{–2})$ near the
surface on that planet is $_____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let time to travel 81 m is t sec.

Time to travel 100 m is t + $\frac{1}{2}$ sec.

$\therefore$ 81 = $\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ a $\times$ $t^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ t = $9\sqrt{\frac{2}{a}}$

And 100 = $\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ a $\times$ $\left (\frac{1}{2}+t\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $t+\frac{1}{2}$ = $10\sqrt{\frac{2}{a}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $9\sqrt{\frac{2}{a}}$ + $\frac{1}{2}$ = $10\sqrt{\frac{2}{a}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{\frac{2}{a}}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $a = 8 m/s^{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Evening Slot

solution.body:
